citation: Zou H, Gao S, Liu X, Liu Y, Xiao Y, Li A, Jiang Y. Combination of metagenomic next-generation sequencing and conventional tests unraveled pathogen profiles in infected patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in Jilin Province of China. Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology. 2024;14:1378112.

population.population_description: Patients undergoing HSCT with suspected infection at First Hospital of Jilin University

specimens.n_tests: 0.6 mL per sample used for DNA extraction (mNGS performed on all 64 patients)

index_test.platform_or_panel: Conventional mNGS and hybridization capture-based targeted mNGS (TIANamp Micro DNA Kit DP316, QIAseq Ultralow Input Library Kit); DNA only

reference_standard: Final clinical diagnoses and causative pathogens independently made by 2-3 clinicians with infectious-disease expertise, using mNGS results (positive and negative), complete laboratory examinations, treatment response, and clinical experience

diagnostic_yield.n_tests: mNGS on all 64 patients; CT on 58 patients
diagnostic_yield.yield_percent: more than 75% of infections were caused by viruses (CMV and EBV most common)
diagnostic_yield.basis: final clinical diagnoses as gold standard; numeric sensitivity/specificity/TCR values are shown only in Figure 5, not in the text

additional_yield_vs_conventional: "Differences in positive rate between mNGS and CT for different samples were found (Figure 4)"; numeric per-sample comparison values are in Figure 4/Supplementary Table S1, not in text. Authors state mNGS performance was not better than CT overall.

quality_flags.blinding_of_index_result: no (final diagnosis explicitly incorporated mNGS results)
quality_flags.overlap_risk: Single center; all patients HSCT; mNGS results part of the adjudication

quadas2_notes: Sensitivity, specificity and total coincidence rate vs final clinical diagnosis are reported only graphically (Figure 5) - no quotable numeric 2x2 in text. Incorporation bias: adjudicators used mNGS results. No TAT reported.

evidence_quotes.quote: From February 2021 to August 2022, 64 patients, admitted to the Department of Hematology of The First Hospital of Jilin University for HSCT and diagnosed as suspected infections, were retrospectively enrolled.
A total of 38 patients were diagnosed as having infections
In our study, mNGS was performed on the whole patients enrolled, while CT was performed on 58 patients
Taking final clinical diagnoses as gold standard, we found that more than 75% of infections were caused by viruses, and CMV and EBV were found to be the most common pathogens.
We found that the performance of mNGS in diagnosing infection was not better than that of CT

According to mNGS results (including both positive and negative mNGS results), complete laboratory examinations, the treatment response of the patients, and clinical experiences, the final clinical diagnoses and causative pathogens were independently made by 2-3 clinicians with expertise in infectious diseases.

evidence_quotes.claim: accuracy evaluated but numeric values in figure only
evidence_quotes.quote: Besides, we also evaluated the performance of mNGS and CT against final clinical diagnosis, including sensitivity, specificity, and total coincidence rate (TCR).
RNA mNGS was not performed on the patients in this study
